slot.subtopic: Perpendicular distance from point to line
slot.brief: Find the foot of the perpendicular from a point to a line given in 3D vector form; ask for the coordinates

stem: The foot of the perpendicular from $P(3,3,2)$ to the line $(x,y,z)=(1,2,-1)+t(2,-1,2)$ is:

verdicts.working: For direction vector v=(2,-1,2), the projection parameter is t=((P-(1,2,-1))·v)/(v·v)=9/9=1. Thus the foot is (1,2,-1)+v=(3,1,1).

working:
Let the foot be $F=(1+2t,2-t,-1+2t)$.\n$(P-F)\cdot(2,-1,2)=0$ gives $2(2-2t)-(1+t)+2(3-2t)=0$, so $t=1$.\nHence $F=(3,1,1)$.

Independent check: For direction vector v=(2,-1,2), the projection parameter is t=((P-(1,2,-1))·v)/(v·v)=9/9=1. Thus the foot is (1,2,-1)+v=(3,1,1).
solution:
For the foot $F=(1+2t,2-t,-1+2t)$, the vector $P-F$ must be perpendicular to the line’s direction $(2,-1,2)$.
$$[P-F]\cdot(2,-1,2)=2(2-2t)-(1+t)+2(3-2t)=0,$$
which gives $t=1$. Hence $F=(3,1,1)$.

draft.distractor_notes: A: takes the line’s given point as the foot.\nB: uses $t=2$ instead of the projection parameter.\nD: uses the projection parameter with the wrong sign.
